name: Nu Romantix
editorial_article: "Nu Romantix" is a landmark electronic album by the prolific British producer DMX Krew, originally released in 1998. Emerging during a time when retro-futuristic synth music was finding a renewed voice, the project stands as a definitive exploration of electro, vocoder-heavy synth-pop, and upbeat, fun-focused dance rhythms. DMX Krew, the primary project of Ed Upton, masterfully blends the stark, machine-driven aesthetic of classic electro with a human, melodic sensibility that feels simultaneously nostalgic and forward-looking. \n\nThroughout the record, Upton utilizes analog synthesizers and vocoded vocals to create a sound that is both technically precise and emotionally resonant. Tracks like "Come to Me" and "Place Called Love" showcase the artist's ability to fuse robotic textures with catchy, pop-structured hooks. The album has aged remarkably well, gaining a reputation among electronic music enthusiasts as one of DMX Krew's finest bodies of work, praised for its clarity, charm, and technical execution. Reissued in later years to a new generation of listeners, "Nu Romantix" remains a cornerstone of the late-90s underground electro scene, capturing the spirit of a producer who helped bridge the gap between dancefloor functionality and idiosyncratic musical composition. It is a quintessential artifact of its era, embodying a specific kind of '80s-inspired, high-fidelity synthesizer romanticism that defined the DMX Krew project.
